title: Lease-epoch redesign and streaming backpressure overhaul for async workers
creator: Asha Patel
description: Refactor the worker lease and retry orchestration to an epoch-based lease model and replace ad-hoc blocking backpressure with a streaming-aware, credit-based flow controller. This reduces head-of-line blocking, prevents stale-lease reprocessing, and makes redis/kafka consumers cooperative under load.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Worker leases use epoch tokens persisted in Redis; 2) In-flight windows are bounded per-tenant and enforceable without blocking event-loop threads; 3) Retry coordinator supports resumable reenqueue with idempotency keys; 4) Latency P95 for small requests improves or stays within 10% of baseline under 2x traffic; 5) Integration test harness simulates bursts and verifies no duplicate processing past 1 minute; 6) Migration runbook exists and tested in staging.
implementation_plan: Phase A: introduce epoch-lease schema in Redis and library helpers (non-breaking). Phase B: implement credit-based flow controller in consumer shim and plumb to worker executors. Phase C: retry coordinator refactor to persist retry state and idempotency markers. Phase D: cutover via dual-read/dual-write and gradual drain. Parallel: add metrics and tracing (lease_epoch, inflight_credits, shed_count).
migration_steps: 1) Deploy epoch-lease helpers off by default. 2) Start writing epoch metadata alongside existing lease key; continue honoring old lease if epoch absent. 3) Enable credit-based controller in canary tenants; monitor shed_count and latency. 4) Enable retry-state persistence for non-canonical retries for canary. 5) Switch primary lease check to epoch token after 48h of stable canary. 6) Remove legacy lease code in follow-up release.
testing_plan: Unit tests for lease acquisition/release, fuzz test for clock skew and overlapping lease takeovers, load test in staging with k6 simulating 3x traffic burst, chaos test by killing worker mid-lease to validate resumable reenqueue, and end-to-end verification against idempotency harness. Add integration test that replays expired-lease scenarios to ensure no double-processing.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy library in runtime-2.6 with feature flag disabled. 2) Enable feature flag for 5 low-traffic tenants. 3) Monitor: inflight_credits, lost_lease_recoveries, p95_latency, duplicate_processing. 4) Gradually ramp to 25% of tenants, then full enable if metrics stable for 72h. 5) Post-rollback steps defined if duplicate_processing > threshold.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Mis-synced epoch values could temporarily orphan tasks. Mitigation: dual-write strategy and lease-grace window; include a reconciliation job to requeue orphaned messages.
Risk: Credit-based controller may underutilize capacity for bursty tenants. Mitigation: adaptive credit refill tuned by burst-profile per-tenant and allow burst up to configured cap.
Risk: Increased Redis metadata writes may raise cost/latency. Mitigation: batch lease writes and TTL tuning; run Redis client upgrade in parallel (see dependencies).
notes: We intentionally keep epoch token opaque to avoid coupling to worker instance topology. Prefer atomic Lua operations for lease takeover to reduce races. Design aligns with recent token-aware priority allocator work but avoids the sticky-shard model to enable elastic scaling.
open_questions: Should we store idempotency markers in Redis or conflated Kafka compaction topic?
What is an acceptable duplicate threshold for sensitive customers?
Do we need a cross-region lease coordinator for multi-region private deployments?
work_log: 2025-11-21: Spike implemented for epoch token atomic swap using Redis EVAL; verified no races in microbench.
2025-11-26: Load test prototype shows 18% reduction in p95 under steady-state but 22% increase during burst without adaptive credits.
2025-12-01: Design review with PM/SDR; agreed to add reconciliation job and dual-write rollout.
2025-12-02: Migration runbook drafted and uploaded to Drive; PR opened for epoch helpers.
